page: Microsoft Azure M64ls is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MS family, configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz, featuring a 38 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 2097 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is consistently low, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core score of 43772.14 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9711.0. Memory performance is notable for large block read-only bandwidth, which reaches a strong 210.73 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%, while small block read-only and large block write bandwidths remain in the average tier.

Given its 512.0 GB memory capacity and 2097 GB local SSD storage, this server is positioned for memory-intensive workloads that do not rely heavily on single-threaded CPU speed. It is suitable for database operations, as reflected in its average Passmark database score of 17739.68 and Redis SET performance of 40.62 million operations per second. The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density for multi-threaded enterprise applications, though it presents a performance tradeoff for single-threaded tasks like gzip compression or text processing, which rank in the bottom 10%.
